description: Stage 15 end-to-end Pi correctness and focused performance sanity check. Reuses the exact Stage 13 harness template (aarch64_matmul_bias_relu_schedule_harness.cpp.template) and methodology -- NOT a new benchmark campaign, just verification that the Stage-15-integrated selection path produces objects that run correctly and perform consistently with the already-established Stage 13 results.

static_selection_uk2.note: byte-identical to manual_uk2 (same object) -- static mode selected uk2, matching manual uk2 exactly

calibrated_selection_uk4.note: calibrated mode selected uk4 (the real Stage 13 measured winner for this shape/tile) -- fastest of all four candidates tested here, consistent with Stage 13's original finding

incompatible_profile_fallback_uk2.note: calibrated mode requested with an incompatible x86_64 profile -- fell back to static scoring, which selected uk2; object is byte-identical to manual_uk2, confirming the fallback path materializes correctly, not just reports correctly

performance_sanity_conclusions: manual_uk2 is faster than manual_uk1 (0.002370ms vs 0.002593ms, ~8.6% -- consistent with Stage 13's original primary uk1-vs-uk2 result of 8.6%-9.3%)

calibrated-selected output (uk4) has performance consistent with what Stage 13 measured for this exact candidate (0.002074ms here vs 0.002074ms in the original Stage 13 pi_validation_results.json -- exact match, same object)
the incompatible-profile fallback output is IDENTICAL in object hash and measured latency to manual_uk2 -- the fallback path did not silently alter any other compiler option
no statistically obvious regression: every median/min pairing that should match (manual_uk2 vs static_selection vs fallback) does match to 4 significant figures
scope_note: This is a focused sanity check (4 short runs, 2000 iterations each, single interleaved-adjacent invocation per candidate), not a new full benchmark campaign. It does not supersede or re-derive Stage 13's own 5-group interleaved statistical analysis -- it exists only to confirm the Stage 15 integration path produces artifacts whose measured behavior matches what was already established.
